dedupe_keys.name: peering testbed for real world bgp experiments

description: This testbed case covers PEERING, a shared facility that lets researchers and teachers run experiments on the live internet's routing system instead of in simulation. PEERING runs routers and servers at universities, research institutions, internet exchange points and the Vultr cloud, which peer by BGP with real networks; experimenters get controlled use of its autonomous system numbers (mainly AS47065, plus seven more) and of IPv4 and IPv6 address blocks, so they can announce and select routes and send and receive traffic without obtaining their own resources. Access is by an experiment proposal under an acceptable use policy that forbids disrupting services outside PEERING, and core results must be published. The system, described in a CoNEXT 2019 paper, has supported studies of BGP poisoning, anycast catchments, route propagation and security, and is funded partly by the National Science Foundation, Google and GENI. Coverage: sites in several continents, ongoing since the early 2010s. Format and access: website, GitHub organisation and PeeringDB entry; free to approved researchers. Caveats: experiments must stay within the testbed's prefixes and rules; it tests routing behaviour, not physical failures. Simulation uses: validating network-flow and routing models against real BGP behaviour, and testing hijack and failover responses. Related records: BGPy and C-BGP simulate BGP, and RIPE RIS, RouteViews and BGPStream observe it.
